subject: Power analysis using simsem: The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric

messages.author: 43c035062b839bde
messages.subject: Power analysis using simsem: The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric
parts:
Dear all,
I would like to investigate power of a relatively straightforward mediation model using simsem. The model has two independent variables, one mediator, and one dependent variable, as can be seen in the figure attached.

Based on the recet paper by Donnelly, Jorgensen, and Rudolph (https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-022-01996-0), I tried to specify standardized regression parameters, with variance of exogenous variance fixed at 1 and correlation at .30 (an hypothetical value). To do so, I tried to specify the residual correlation as a PS matrix for the exogenous part, using the all-Y LISREL notation (which I used in the old days!).

However, this approach was incorrect, since I get the following error message:

Errore in buildModel(paramSet, modelType) :
  The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric!

To my understanding, this is due to correlation between residuals of the two exogenous variables, but I was not able to find a solution (I tried the command symmetric = FALSE, but did not work).

You can see my syntax below, thanks for any advice.

Best,
Salvatore

***

#load simsem
library(simsem)

#set N
N <- 125

#set mediation parameters
a1 <- .30
a2 <- .30
b <- .30
c1 <- .10
c2 <- .10

#set beta.pop equal beta.free
beta.pop <- beta.free <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = 4, dimnames = list( c("Y","M", "X1", "X2"), c("Y","M", "X1", "X2")))

#Populate beta.free
beta.free["Y", "M"] <- "b"
beta.free["Y", "X1"] <- "c1"
beta.free["Y", "X2"] <- "c2"
beta.free["M", "X1"] <- "a1"
beta.free["M", "X2"] <- "a2"

#Populate beta.pop
beta.pop["Y", "M"] <- b
beta.pop["Y", "X1"] <- c1
beta.pop["Y", "X2"] <- c2
beta.pop["M", "X1"] <- a1
beta.pop["M", "X2"] <- a2

#Create SimMatrix
endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)

#Create correlation matrix of residuals
resid.pop <- resid.free <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = 4, dimnames = list(c("Y","M", "X1", "X2"), c("Y","M", "X1", "X2")))
resid.free[1,1] <- as.numeric(NA)
resid.free[2,2] <- as.numeric(NA)
resid.free[3,3] <- 1 #fixed at 1
resid.free[4,4] <- 1 #fixed at 1
resid.free[4,3] <- .3 #fixed at .3
resid.free[3,4] <- .3 #fixed at .3, try to fix the "RPS symmetric problem"
resid.pop <- diag(4)
resid.pop[4,3] <- .3
resid.pop[3,4] <- .3 #try to fix the "RPS symmetric problem"
residCor <- binds(free = resid.free, popParam = resid.pop, symmetric = FALSE)

#Set user parameters
userParams<-'
ind1 := a1*b
ind2 := a2*b
total1 := ind1+c1
total2 := ind2+c2
'

#Create SimSem model
simMod1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor, con = userParams, indLab = rownames(beta.free))

Errore in buildModel(paramSet, modelType) :
  The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric!

messages.subject: Re: Power analysis using simsem: The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric
parts: using the all-Y LISREL notation (which I used in the old days!)
I tried the command symmetric = FALSE, but did not work

But it ought to be symmetric, so leave it TRUE.  In fact, the binds(...) function is simply bind(..., symmetric = TRUE)

You can also change
resid.pop <- diag(4)
to 
diag(resid.pop) <- 1
in order to preserve the names from when it was created above.

And did you purposely fix the exogenous (co)variances rather than estimate them (by setting them NA in resid.free)?

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics

messages.subject: Re: Power analysis using simsem: The correlation (RPS) matrix must be symmetric
parts:
With these three lines of code, I was trying to fix the correlation between the two exogenous variables at .30, which I think should affect regression parameters. In fact, there is no 'X1~~X2' parameter in the output above, but perhaps this parameter is not necessary in the model?

Below you can see the revised code.

Thank you for your support
Salvatore

##############################
#Model syntax
##############################

#set NULL BETA matrix
#beta.pop equal beta.free

beta.pop <- beta.free <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = 4, dimnames = list( c("Y","M", "X1", "X2"), c("Y","M", "X1", "X2")))

#Populate beta.free
beta.free["Y", "M"] <- "b"
beta.free["Y", "X1"] <- "c1"
beta.free["Y", "X2"] <- "c2"
beta.free["M", "X1"] <- "a1"
beta.free["M", "X2"] <- "a2"

#Populate beta.pop
beta.pop["Y", "M"] <- b
beta.pop["Y", "X1"] <- c1
beta.pop["Y", "X2"] <- c2
beta.pop["M", "X1"] <- a1
beta.pop["M", "X2"] <- a2

#Create SimMatrix
endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)

#Create correlation matrix of residuals
resid.pop <- resid.free <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = 4, dimnames = list(c("Y","M", "X1", "X2"), c("Y","M", "X1", "X2")))
resid.free[1,1] <- as.numeric(NA)
resid.free[2,2] <- as.numeric(NA)

resid.free[3,3] <- as.numeric(NA) #residuals variace exogenous variable freely estimated
resid.free[4,4] <- as.numeric(NA) #residuals variace exogenous variable freely estimated

#resid.pop <- diag(4)
diag(resid.pop) <- 1
residCor <- binds(free = resid.free, popParam = resid.pop)

#Set user parameters
#indirect/total effects

userParams<-'
ind1 := a1*b
ind2 := a2*b
total1 := ind1+c1
total2 := ind2+c2
'

#Create SimSem model
simMod1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor, con = userParams, indLab = rownames(beta.free))

#Custom function to obtain
#MCCCIs for indirect effects
rejectMCCI <- function(object) {
CIs <- semTools::monteCarloCI(object)
apply(CIs, 1, function(CI) 0 < CI["ci.lower"] | 0 > CI["ci.upper"])
}

#Run simulatiom
#nRep should be 5000
out1<-sim(nRep=1000, model=simMod1, n=N, seed = 12345, outfun = rejectMCCI)

#Inspect nonconvergent replications
summary(out1)

#Get power,
summaryParam(out1, matchParam = TRUE, digits = 3)

#Empirical estimate of power for Monte Carlo CIs
testMCCI <- do.call(rbind, getExtraOutput(out1))
colMeans(testMCCI)
